about.title: Danville Slip & Fall & Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Danville draws steady foot traffic to its shopping plazas, downtown restaurants, and neighborhood complexes tucked near Camino Tassajara and the I-680 corridor. When a property owner lets a spill sit too long, skips lighting repairs, or ignores a cracked walkway, everyday visitors can end up seriously hurt. California law doesn't hand you a claim just because you fell — you generally need to show the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix it or warn you. That's why documentation matters from the first moment: photos of the condition, names of witnesses, and a request to preserve any surveillance footage before it's overwritten. LawProactive isn't a law firm — we're a free connection service that puts injured Danville residents in touch with independent attorneys who work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless your case results in a recovery. If a fall has disrupted your life, it's worth having someone experienced look at what happened.

whyChoose.title: Why Talking to an Attorney Early Matters

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard before your fall. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records that establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Danville businesses overwrite security video within days or weeks. Acting quickly to send a preservation request can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Eliminate, Recovery
items.desc: Even if you're partly at fault for not noticing a hazard, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows a claim — your potential recovery is simply adjusted to reflect your share of responsibility.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Danville?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity — a public building or park, for instance — the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. It's best to have a claim reviewed well before any deadline approaches.

items.question: What if the store or apartment complex says I wasn't paying attention?
items.answer: That's a common response, but it doesn't automatically end your claim. California's comparative fault rules allow for shared responsibility, meaning your recovery may be reduced but not necessarily eliminated. An independent attorney can help evaluate how much that argument actually affects your case.

items.question: Does it matter that my fall happened near a busy area like Camino Tassajara?
items.answer: Location itself doesn't determine fault, but it can affect how many witnesses, cameras, or nearby businesses might have relevant evidence. Higher-traffic areas of Danville sometimes mean more potential documentation, which can help support your claim.

items.question: Is there a cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost to have your situation reviewed.
